construct: empty and whitespace-only bash command detection — the ability to recognize that a bash tool invocation with an empty or whitespace-only command string should be blocked before executing any shell process, preventing wasted resources and meaningless shell invocations.

input.description: The agent issues a bash tool call where the command string is empty or contains only whitespace characters.
setup: Agent calls bash tool with command=""
ToolGuard inspects the command before execution
ToolGuard determines the command is effectively empty and blocks it

expectedBehavior: ToolGuard blocks the invocation entirely — no shell process is spawned, and a block signal is recorded with ruleName='empty_bash'.
failureImplication: Empty or whitespace-only bash commands are sent to the shell, wasting resources and potentially causing unexpected side effects.
relatedPaper: AHE: regression prediction accuracy only 11.8%, explicit blocking of known-bad patterns is essential.
regressionRisk: Changes to command trimming logic or ToolGuard rule ordering could allow whitespace-only commands to pass through.
